blocks.text: Westwood Plateau: streets and boundaries

items.t: Westwood Plateau is the planned residential plateau on Eagle Mountain in north Coquitlam, reached from below by Johnson Street and by Plateau Boulevard and Parkway Boulevard climbing the slope.

The City's own history in the Interim Official Community Plan (OCP), Bylaw No. 5511, 2026 records that the Westwood Racing Circuit opened in 1959 at the end of Johnson Street on Eagle Mountain and closed in 1990 to make way for residential development on Westwood Plateau.

Scott Creek and Eagle Ridge sit below the plateau to the south, Port Moody is the municipal neighbour to the west, and Anmore lies beyond the city boundary to the northwest — adjacency as shown on City and TransLink route mapping for the Johnson Street corridor.

blocks.text: Westwood Plateau: the housing stock

items.t: What is specific to the plateau is its planned form: a single master-planned subdivision era on a mountain bench, with the golf course lands and greenbelts threaded between residential streets rather than a grid of older lots.
Summit Middle School at 1450 Parkway Boulevard is the middle school building on the plateau itself, opened as part of the plateau's build-out to serve the new population on Eagle Mountain.

blocks.text: Westwood Plateau: rules that affect buyers

items.t: The Interim OCP carries four development permit areas city-wide: Urban Design, Watercourse Protection, Wildfire Hazard and Unstable Slopes, with maps in Schedule G and guidelines in Schedule H.

Single-family dwellings do not require a form and character development permit, but a permit is still required before subdividing, constructing or adding to a building on land inside a development permit area.

blocks.text: Westwood Plateau: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: The Coquitlam Crunch Trail tops out on Westwood Plateau: it climbs 2.2 kilometres on the British Columbia Hydro right-of-way with 894 steps and 242 metres of elevation gain, and its access points include Bramble Park on Panorama Drive and David Avenue.

Route 187's plateau loop is one-directional in effect: outbound buses climb Johnson Street to Plateau Boulevard and Paddock Drive, and the return runs from Parkway Boulevard at Plateau Boulevard back down Johnson Street to Coquitlam Central Station.
Route 185 also touches the plateau's south edge, running Lansdowne Drive to Panorama Drive below the plateau before continuing as the 184 toward Moody Centre Station.

The City tells small-scale housing applicants to contact Development Services before designing if there is a creek on or next to the lot or a steep slope on or next to it — both are common conditions on plateau edge lots.

blocks.text: Westwood Plateau: costs and taxes

items.t: Coquitlam is a designated taxable area for the provincial Speculation and Vacancy Tax, so a plateau owner must complete the annual declaration.

blocks.text: Westwood Plateau: getting around

items.t: There is no SkyTrain or West Coast Express station in or beside the plateau; both are reached at Coquitlam Central Station, the route 187 terminus.
Johnson Street is the main road off the plateau, connecting south to Guildford Way and the City Centre; Plateau Boulevard and Parkway Boulevard are the internal plateau arterials the bus loop uses.

blocks.text: Westwood Plateau: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check the Wildfire Hazard and Unstable Slopes development permit maps in OCP Schedule G first for any forest-edge or slope lot; the schedules show the layers, not a lot-level geotechnical conclusion.

Check the City environmental development permit mapping, Schedule B, which maps environmentally sensitive areas, steep slopes and the interface wildfire boundary for the City Centre and Northeast areas.

Check watercourse distance before planning any addition: within 30 metres of top of bank or ravine bank in this part of the city, a Watercourse Protection Development Permit is required before land is altered.

blocks.text: Westwood Plateau home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

57 houses sold in Westwood Plateau with a median price of $1,740,000 (the middle half sold between $1,630,000 and $1,900,000), taking a median of 30 days to sell at 95.9% of the last list price; 2% sold above list. They had a median $444 per square foot, a median year built of 1994 and a median lot of 6,996 square feet. 44 condos sold in Westwood Plateau with a median price of $656,500 (the middle half sold between $617,500 and $715,575), taking a median of 24 days to sell at 97.4% of the last list price; 2% sold above list. They had a median $689 per square foot, a median year built of 2008 and a median strata fee of $487 a month.

faq.q: How many homes are for sale in Westwood Plateau?
faq.a: At the end of October 2026 the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® figures showed 57 houses and 48 condos and townhomes listed in Westwood Plateau. Those are month-end counts and they move daily, so ask Jared for a current list.

faq.q: Is Westwood Plateau a buyers’ or sellers’ market?
faq.a: In October 2026, houses had a sales ratio of 14% (a balanced market); condos and townhomes had 13% (a balanced market). The sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed; on the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers. One month in one community is a small sample, so look at the monthly table above before you decide.

faq.q: How many homes sold in Westwood Plateau from June to October 2026?
faq.a: 40 houses and 41 condos and townhomes sold in Westwood Plateau over those 5 months; detached houses peaked in June with 12 sold and condos and townhomes peaked in June with 13 sold.

faq.q: How big is Westwood Plateau compared with the rest of Coquitlam?
faq.a: In October 2026, Westwood Plateau held 15.1% of the 378 detached houses listed in Coquitlam and 6.2% of the 779 condos and townhomes listed in Coquitlam.

faq.q: What mix of houses and condos is for sale in Westwood Plateau?
faq.a: In October 2026, houses made up 54.3% of the 105 homes listed in Westwood Plateau and condos and townhomes made up 45.7%; of the 14 that sold, houses were 57.1% and condos and townhomes 42.9%.

faq.q: Are there more or fewer homes for sale in Westwood Plateau than in June?
faq.a: Listings of detached houses fell from 61 in June to 57 in October 2026 (−6.6%); condos and townhomes fell from 53 in June to 48 in October 2026 (−9.4%).

faq.q: Is there a SkyTrain station on Westwood Plateau?
faq.a: No, there is no rapid transit on the plateau. The transit link is TransLink route 187, which runs from Coquitlam Central Station up Johnson Street, then Plateau Boulevard, Paddock Drive and Plateau Boulevard again to Parkway Boulevard at Plateau Boulevard. Every plateau trip to the Millennium Line or the West Coast Express starts with that bus leg or a drive down Johnson Street.

faq.q: Which elementary schools serve plateau addresses?
faq.a: Catchment is by home address in School District No. 43 (SD43), and the plateau's named elementary building is Bramblewood Elementary at 2875 Panorama Drive.

faq.q: Does the wildfire interface affect a plateau lot?
faq.a: It can, because the Interim OCP designates a Wildfire Hazard Development Permit Area and maps it in Schedule G, and the plateau's forest-edge and greenbelt lots are the ones to check against that map. The permit area does not ban building; it sets conditions through the Schedule H guidelines, and the map — not the street name — decides whether a specific lot is inside it.

faq.q: What happened to the land before the houses?
faq.a: It was a racetrack. The City records that the Westwood Racing Circuit opened in 1959 at the end of Johnson Street on Eagle Mountain, was the first purpose-built permanent road course in Canada, and closed in 1990 to make way for residential development on Westwood Plateau. That history explains the plateau's single-era, master-planned street pattern.

faq.q: What did houses in Westwood Plateau sell for?
faq.a: 57 houses sold in Westwood Plateau between November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026, with a median price of $1,740,000.

faq.q: How long do houses take to sell in Westwood Plateau?
faq.a: The median was 30 days from listing to sale, and homes sold at a median 95.9% of the last list price (2% sold above list), for sales November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026.
